request.current_synthesis: Established by the fixed scientific model: the plant is deterministic, fully actuated, and sensed with joint position, joint velocity, target displacement, and analytic IK-branch errors. The consequential mechanisms are bounded, configuration-dependent actuation; inertial coordination during approach and braking; and a narrow tolerance band requiring low residual end-effector motion for 2 seconds. Two competing explanations remain: failures may be dominated by reachability and branch selection across the full radius-angle distribution, or policies may reach geometrically but fail from overshoot, oscillation, or insufficient stabilizing authority inside the band. The model makes the second mechanism especially credible because the hold is long relative to the 20 ms action interval, but no campaign observation establishes which mechanism dominates. The current training distribution is also narrower than the official radial distribution, creating a separate coverage risk. No claim about learned performance or official success is justified yet.
request.decision_frontier: In the first goal-linked inquiry, discriminate reach/coverage limitation from stabilization limitation in the first learned policy. Evidence that separates them is a completed fixed-seed evaluation with per-episode target radius and angle, first in-tolerance step, maximum uninterrupted held steps, hold interruptions, and minimum/final distance, interpreted against the baseline training distribution and the official development distribution. Predominantly late first reach or geometry-correlated failures would support a coverage/trajectory direction; early reach followed by short holds and repeated interruptions would support a stabilization-aware learning direction. A mixed pattern would require identifying the dominant subgroup before intervention.

T3 therefore missed the 196/200 threshold by 196 episodes and cannot support the official 98% objective. The intervention also had zero training success across all checkpoints, so it provides no evidence that stronger endpoint-speed shaping improves stabilization. Retain T1:checkpoint-100352 as the strongest evidence-backed development candidate and do not request official assessment.

request.candidates_and_roles: T1:checkpoint-100352 remains the strongest evidence-backed development candidate and baseline reference at 189/200, supported by M1, M2, and M3. T2:checkpoint-120832 remains a measured but insufficient intervention at 176/200 with 19 post-entry hold failures. T3:checkpoint-120832 is a measured failed stabilization recipe at 0/200 and has no role. No candidate has been assigned working, best-known, or retained status.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Three fresh PPO training operations completed with the maintainer's requested 120000-step allocation, each producing 120832 rollout-boundary steps. M1 evaluated T1 on the 200-episode panel [4200, 4400); M2 evaluated T2 and T1 on that same paired panel; M3 evaluated T3 and T1 on that same paired panel. No official assessment has been run.
request.current_goal_gap: T1:checkpoint-100352 remains the strongest supported development result at 189/200 (94.5%), seven successes below the 196/200 development objective. T2:checkpoint-120832 achieved 176/200 and increased post-entry hold failures from 5 to 19. T3:checkpoint-120832 achieved 0/200, with zero training success across all T3 checkpoints. No candidate supports an official 98% claim.
request.current_synthesis: T1 established a reproducible baseline whose failures were concentrated in the -180 to -90 degree sector: six failures never entered tolerance and five entered but held only 1-2 samples. I2's coupled focused-sampling and compatible-branch intervention eliminated that sector's acquisition failures but traded them for more post-entry hold failures, so complete success remained worse. I3 isolated stabilization by restoring baseline full-angle target sampling and open/folded IK-branch observations while doubling endpoint-speed shaping. T3 failed to learn at every checkpoint and scored 0/200 complete successes, versus T1's reproduced 189/200 on the same paired panel. This resolves the tested stronger speed-shaping recipe as insufficient, but does not prove that all stabilization-aware methods are ineffective. The evidence is development-only; the official objective remains unmeasured.
request.decision_frontier: I3 is resolved as insufficient. At the next fresh goal-review session, decide whether a new bounded, evidence-backed mechanism can address the remaining angular acquisition and complete-hold gap without repeating the tested tradeoffs, or whether no credible route remains. Any future candidate must be judged by complete uninterrupted success and post-entry failures, not tolerance entry alone; official assessment is not justified by the current evidence.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 complete uninterrupted holds in a 200-episode official panel. I3 did not establish a route to that goal: T3 achieved 0/200 on the fixed development panel, while the paired T1 reference achieved 189/200. The official-distribution objective remains unmeasured and unclaimed.
request.next_direction_or_closure: This inquiry is closed as insufficient and the session is ending. Return to goal review in a fresh session. Do not request official assessment from the current evidence; first determine whether a scientifically credible new route remains, with T1 preserved as the reference.

request.closure_condition: Train one fresh 120000-step candidate with only the normalized hold-progress observation added to the T1 recipe, then compare it with T1 on the fixed 200-episode development panel. Close the inquiry as insufficient if complete successes do not improve over 189/200 or if post-entry failures improve only by introducing a material regression in the -180 to -90 degree acquisition sector; redirect only if the paired diagnostics identify a different dominant mechanism.
request.goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 complete uninterrupted holds in a 200-episode official panel. T1 reaches 189/200 development successes, with five post-entry hold failures and six angular acquisition failures. Making the temporal phase observable tests whether the remaining hold failures arise from the current policy's inability to condition stabilization on hold progress, while preserving the acquisition recipe that T1 supports.
request.question: Can exposing normalized uninterrupted-hold progress to the policy, while preserving T1's full-angle target distribution and analytic branch observations, reduce complete-hold failures without sacrificing angular acquisition?
request.rationale: The physical model identifies the 2-second hold as a temporal control requirement, but the current 11-value memoryless observation omits hold progress. T3 tested stronger endpoint-speed reward shaping and collapsed to zero success, while I2's acquisition intervention traded angular failures for hold failures. A phase-progress observation is a distinct, low-confounding intervention that preserves T1's sampling, branch inputs, reward, and torque interface, and its paired result directly tests whether temporal observability can close the complete-hold gap.

request.current_synthesis: T1 shows that full-angle sampling and open/folded IK-branch observations can produce a reproducible near-goal policy, but residual failures combine angular acquisition with incomplete stabilization. I2 eliminated the diagnosed acquisition sector failures only by trading them for substantially more post-entry failures, so that coupled intervention is insufficient. I3's isolated stronger endpoint-speed shaping failed to learn and does not establish that all stabilization-aware mechanisms are ineffective. A consequential competing explanation remains: the plant may be controllable from the existing state, but a memoryless policy lacks explicit temporal phase information needed to condition its regulation during a 100-sample uninterrupted hold. I4 tests that explanation while preserving T1's acquisition recipe. All evidence remains development-only and does not establish official performance.

request.description: Train one fresh PPO candidate with the T1 full-angle target distribution, analytic open/folded IK-branch observations, reward, and dynamics unchanged, while appending normalized uninterrupted hold progress (held steps divided by the 100-step requirement) to the policy observation.
request.rationale: I4 tests whether the remaining post-entry failures reflect missing temporal phase information rather than insufficient physical state. The intervention exposes only the current uninterrupted hold progress, resets it to zero on episode reset or any tolerance exit, and leaves target sampling, branch observations, reward, action interface, and task mechanics unchanged. A fresh seed-0 run under the maintainer's fixed 120000-step allocation is required for a direct comparison with T1. The resulting candidate will be evaluated on the same fixed 200-episode development panel using complete success, post-entry failures, and the -180 to -90 degree acquisition subgroup.
